description: Mistakes agents repeat with shell pipelines, loops and monitors

pipe-status.description: A pipeline ending in a filter whose status is branched on or read as if it were the producer's
pipe-status.message: A pipeline's status is its last command's (`{LAST}`), so a failure of the first command goes unseen. Run `set -o pipefail` first, or write to a file, check the status, then read the file.
pipe-status.messageShort: Pipe status is `{LAST}`'s. `set -o pipefail`, or write to a file and check it.

messages.text: `$?` after a pipe is the last command's status. Use `set -o pipefail` first, or read zsh `pipestatus[1]` / bash `PIPESTATUS[0]` in the very next command.
messages.messageShort: `$?` is the last stage's. `set -o pipefail`, or `pipestatus[1]` (zsh) / `PIPESTATUS[0]` (bash).

messages.text: `head` hides the producer's status, and `set -o pipefail` would report SIGPIPE (141) when `head` closes early. Write to a file, check the status, then `head` the file.
messages.messageShort: `head` hides the producer's status; pipefail gives 141. Write to a file, check it, then `head` it.

pipe-status-filter.description: A pipeline ending in a display filter (cat, sort, sed, ...) whose status is branched on or read as if it were the producer's
pipe-status-filter.message: A pipeline's status is its last command's (`{LAST}`), so a failure of the first command is masked here. Run `set -o pipefail` first, or write to a file, check the status, then read the file.
pipe-status-filter.messageShort: Pipe status is `{LAST}`'s. `set -o pipefail`, or write to a file and check it.

messages.text: `$?` after a pipe is the last command's status. Use `set -o pipefail` first, or read zsh `pipestatus[1]` / bash `PIPESTATUS[0]` in the very next command.
messages.messageShort: `$?` is the last stage's. `set -o pipefail`, or `pipestatus[1]` (zsh) / `PIPESTATUS[0]` (bash).

pipe-status-chain.description: A pipeline ending in a filter whose status gates a following `&&`
pipe-status-chain.message: `&&` after this pipeline tests `{LAST}`'s status, so a failure of the first command is masked and the command after `&&` may run anyway. Run `set -o pipefail` first, read `PIPESTATUS`, or run the producer on its own.
pipe-status-chain.messageShort: `&&` tests `{LAST}`'s status only, so the next command may run after a failure. `set -o pipefail`.

ps-grep-self-match.description: ps piped into grep, awk or sed without a self-match guard
ps-grep-self-match.message:
`ps … | grep X` (or `awk '/X/'`, `sed -n '/X/p'`) lists the filter itself and your own shell (the tool wraps each command in `zsh -c … eval '…'`, which contains the pattern too), so the output has two false lines.
Add `| grep -v grep` AFTER the match, or bracket the pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`: the bracketed pattern does not match its own command line), or use `pgrep -fl '[c]argo'` as its own command.
ps-grep-self-match.messageShort: `ps | grep X` also lists the grep itself and your own shell: `| grep -v grep` after the match, a bracketed pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`), or `pgrep -fl '[c]argo'` on its own.

messages.text:
The count is off by about 2: `ps … | grep X` also counts the grep itself and your own shell (the tool wraps each command in `zsh -c … eval '…'`, which contains the pattern too).
Add `| grep -v grep` AFTER the match, or bracket the pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`), before counting.
messages.messageShort: `ps | grep X` also counts the grep itself and your own shell, so a count is off by about 2: `| grep -v grep` after the match, or bracket the pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`).

messages.text:
The PID you extract may be the grep's or your own shell's, not the process you meant: `ps … | grep X` also lists both (the tool wraps each command in `zsh -c … eval '…'`, which contains the pattern too). Read the output and confirm the PID (`ps -p PID -o command=`) before you use it.
Add `| grep -v grep` AFTER the match, or bracket the pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`), so only the real process is left.
messages.messageShort: The extracted PID may be the grep's or your shell's: confirm it (`ps -p PID -o command=`) before using it; `| grep -v grep` after the match or a bracketed pattern (`grep '[c]argo'`) leaves only the real process.

tail-pipe-buffered.description: a command stage that may buffer its output after a streaming source in a Monitor
tail-pipe-buffered.message:
A stage after `tail -f` that is not line-buffered may hold its output until its buffer fills, so the Monitor can stay silent.
Make the stage line-buffered: `grep --line-buffered`, `sed -u`, `tr -u`, `awk '{{print; fflush()}}'`, `jq --unbuffered`, `stdbuf -oL cut ...`.

http-wait-exact-status.description: a loop that waits for one specific 2xx status from curl
http-wait-exact-status.message:
Do not wait for one specific success code: a 404, 401 or 3xx never becomes 200, so the loop spins until its timeout.
Loop only while the status is 000 or 5xx, stop on anything else and read the code (`case $c in 000|5??) sleep 2;; *) echo $c; break;; esac`), or let curl retry: `curl --retry N --retry-connrefused -s -o /dev/null -w '%{{http_code}}' URL` (--retry only retries timeouts and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504).
